text.p: Talley Industries Inc said Tuesday that two of its long standing directors were ousted and replaced by directors supported by dissident shareholders.
Tally said in a statement directors Townsend Hoopes and William Mallender were replaced in a shareholder vote by Robert Craig and Ralph Rockow.

Craig and Rockow were both backed by a group called SCREAM (Shareholders Committee to Remove Entrenched and Arrogant Management) which is led by dissident shareholder Saad Alissa. Alissa has held about eight or nine percent of Talley's stock since 1994 and is unhappy with its performance when compared to the S&P 500 index, company spokesman Dan Mullen said.
A third new director, Paul Foster who was supported by both management and the dissident shareholders, was also elected.
The vote leaves the dissident shareholders with control of just two of the company's 10 board seats, Mullen said adding that he does not expect the vote to result in any executive changes.
Mallender lost his seat on the board, which he had held since 1974, but will remain as Talley's chief executive officer. Hoopes, who had been on the board since 1978, was a non-executive director.
